chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Takbir is obligatory at the end of every obligatory or voluntary prayer during the days of Tashriq.

His saying (peace be upon him) 'The Takbir is obligatory' means that he intended the emphasis of the Sunnah. And we have explained in other places that this is called obligatory, even if it is not a duty for which one incurs punishment by leaving it. This clarifies what we mentioned, what he narrated:

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.وَاجِبٌ: Obligatory (a specific level of legal ruling in Shia fiqh, often less strict than fard but more emphasized than sunnah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting the Takbir after prayers during the days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential status of the *Takbir al-Tarawih* (or *Takbir al-Mu'allaq*) recited after the five daily prayers during the Days of Tashriq. The scholar explains that while technically an emphasized Sunnah (*Sunnah Mu'akkadah*), it is termed 'obligatory' (*wajib*) in this specific context to denote its high importance, distinguishing it from a strict duty (*fard*) where omission incurs punishment. This ruling underscores the communal and ritualistic emphasis on glorifying God during the Hajj season, linking the individual prayer to the broader Hajj rites.
